    StartersCharles's running late canapésSmoked salmon blinis, and asparagus spears wrapped in crisp prosciuttoHow to make it16 blinis200g smoked salmon200ml crème fraîche1 bunch dill1 bunch asparagus100g prosciuttoTrim the asparagus and blanch for a minute.Blanch.Wrap each spear in prosciutto and grill until crisp.Top the blinis with crème fraîche, salmon and dill.Arrange both on trays.Smoked salmon oatcakesOatcakes with cream cheese, smoked salmon, dill and lemonHow to make it1 packet oatcakes250g cream cheese200g smoked salmon1 bunch dill1 lemonSpread the oatcakes with cream cheese.Top with folds of salmon and a sprig of dill.Squeeze over a little lemon and lay on a slate.Lucky Boatman ploughman's boardThe old pub where Charles and Carrie stay the nightHow to make itAs written, serves 4Aged cheddar, thick-cut ham, sharp pickled onions, a jammy egg with mustard salt and tomato chutney, with crusty bread, cold butter and apple.Boil 4 eggs for 7 minutes, cool in iced water, peel, halve and sprinkle with salt mixed with a pinch of mustard powder.Cut 250g aged cheddar into thick wedges and fold 200g thick-cut ham onto a big board.Add 8 pickled onions, a bowl of tomato chutney, 1 sliced green apple tossed in lemon, a handful of watercress and the eggs.Slice a crusty loaf thickly and serve with a block of cold butter.MainsEnglish wedding roast beefBeef topside, Yorkshire puddings baked in muffin tins, roast potatoesHow to make it1.5kg beef topside150g plain flour3 eggs300ml full cream milk1kg potatoes3 tbsp vegetable oil500ml beef stockSeason the beef. Whisk the flour, eggs and milk into a batter and rest it.Roast the beef at 200°C to medium.Peel and chop the potatoes, toss them in some of the vegetable oil and put them in alongside.Rest the beef. Heat the muffin tins with the rest of the vegetable oil.Pour in the batter and bake.Make gravy from the pan juices and stock.Highland braised lamb, neeps and tattiesThe Scottish wedding feastHow to make itAs written, serves 4Lamb shoulder braised 3 hours with onion, carrots and barley, with mashed neeps and tatties.Season 1.5kg lamb shoulder and brown all over in a heavy pot.Add 2 chopped onions, 3 carrots in chunks, 75g pearl barley, rosemary and 750ml chicken stock.Cover and braise at 160°C for 3 hours until it pulls apart.Boil 800g peeled potatoes and 600g swede separately until soft.Mash the potatoes with 50g butter and a splash of milk and the swede with 30g butter and pepper.Serve the lamb and barley over both with the juices.SweetsFour weddings lemon curd cakeLemon sponge layers filled with lemon curd and whipped creamHow to make it250g butter250g caster sugar4 eggs1 lemon250g self-raising flour1 jar lemon curd300ml thickened cream200g icing sugar1 handful of fresh edible flowersHeat the oven to 175°C and prepare two tins. Beat the butter and sugar, add the eggs and lemon zest, then fold in the flour.Bake in two tins.Cool completely.Whip the cream and sandwich with lemon curd and cream.Ice white with icing sugar and water and decorate with flowers.DrinksGareth's waistcoat elderflower fizzElderflower cordial and lemon in a flute with a cucumber ribbon, topped with bubblesHow to make it1 Lebanese cucumber80ml elderflower cordial1 lemon750ml sparkling wine750ml sparkling waterPeel the cucumber into long ribbons and curl one into each of four glasses.Add cordial and a squeeze of lemon to each.Top slowly with cold sparkling wine.For drivers, use sparkling water and a little extra cordial.
